answer: The lantern chain is verified at intake and dune publishes each anchor. A newly minted alias has no such history, which means it must survive 3 epochs before its first payout, and abandoning it forfeits the wait. To earn at all, an identity must present a signature chain reaching back to a settlement at least 3 epochs old, anchored at a cipher checkpoint. That bill is paid per identity, so 316 aliases cost 160 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
